Commentary of al-Qasimi (*Mahasin al-Ta'wil*) on Surah 81, verses 1–9 (part 1 of 2):

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surat at-Takwir

It is also called the surah of ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾. It is Meccan, and its verses number twenty-nine.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn Umar that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look upon the Day of Resurrection as if he were seeing it with his own eyes, let him recite ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾ [Al-Infitar: 1] and ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq: 1]." At-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1–9] ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ ﴿And when the stars fall and scatter﴾ [At-Takwir: 2] ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾ [At-Takwir: 3] ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾ [At-Takwir: 4] ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [At-Takwir: 5] ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [At-Takwir: 6] ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [At-Takwir: 7] ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾ [At-Takwir: 8] ﴿for what sin she was killed﴾ [At-Takwir: 9]

﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: that is, it is removed from its place, cast off from its orbit, and its light is extinguished.

﴿And when the stars fall and scatter﴾ [At-Takwir: 2]: that is, they are scattered and plunge down.

﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾ [At-Takwir: 3]: that is, they are lifted from the surface of the earth and blown away, because of the quaking and the earthquake that shatters their joints.

﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾ [At-Takwir: 4]: that is, they are left neglected, with no herdsman and no one to claim them. ''Al-'Isharu'' is the plural of ''ushara'', which is a she-camel whose pregnancy has reached ten months. He singled them out because they are the most precious of their possessions. That is: when these pregnant animals, for which their owners compete, are neglected and left alone because of the severity of the terror that has descended upon them, then what of other things?!

﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [At-Takwir: 5]: that is, they are brought together from every side and mixed together, because the earthquake and the destruction have overtaken their dens and hiding places, so they come out bewildered and terrified, from the effect of the earthquake of the earth, and their joints are torn apart.

﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [At-Takwir: 6]: that is, they are filled by some of them being made to flow into others, until they become one single sea. It derives from ''sajjara al-tannur'', meaning he filled the oven with firewood. Like His saying: ﴿And when the seas are made to burst forth﴾ [Al-Infitar: 3]. It has also been said that the meaning is that they blaze into fire. Al-Qaffal said: It is possible that Hell lies in the depths of the seas, and it is not kindled now for the sake of the continuation of the world. When the term of the world is complete, God will convey the effect of those fires to the seas, and they will become entirely kindled because of that. Al-Imam clarified this by saying: Their being set ablaze may also mean their being ignited into fire. For what is within the belly of the earth of fire will appear at that time, through its splitting open and the tearing apart of its upper layers, while the water at that point turns into vapour, and nothing remains in the seas except fire. As for the belly of the earth containing fire, some reports have indicated this. It has been reported that "the sea is the covering of Hell," though this is not found in its authentic collections. Yet scientific research has established it, and the boiling of volcanoes, which are mountains of fire, bears witness to it. End of quotation.

Al-Razi said: Know that these six signs may occur at the beginning of the time of the destruction of the world, and they may also occur after the Resurrection has taken place. There is nothing in the wording that indicates either of the two possibilities. As for the remaining six, they are specific to the Resurrection. End of quotation.

﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [At-Takwir: 7]: that is, the spirits are joined to their bodies, or they are gathered together with their likes in good and evil, and they are classified into categories, so that each is gathered with those who resemble him, among the blessed and the wretched.

﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾ [At-Takwir: 8] ﴿for what sin she was killed﴾ [At-Takwir: 9]: meaning the daughters whom groups of the Arabs used to kill. Al-Sayyid al-Murtada said in his ''Amali'': The ''mawudah'' is the one who was killed while still young. The Arabs in the Jahiliyyah used to bury their daughters, by burying them alive. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Shall he keep it in disgrace, or bury it in the dust?﴾ [An-Nahl: 59], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those have lost who killed their children foolishly, without knowledge﴾ [Al-An'am: 140]. It is said that they used to do this for two reasons. One of them is that they would kill them out of fear of poverty. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not kill your children out of poverty﴾ [Al-An'am: 151]. Al-Murtada said: I found Abu 'Ali al-Jubba'i and others saying: She was only called ''mawudah'' because the dirt that was thrown upon her weighed her down until she died. In this there is some room for consideration, because they say from ''mawudah'' ''wada'a (yadi'u) wa'dan'', and the agent is ''wa'id'', and the feminine agent is ''wa'idah''. And from weight they say: ''ada'ni al-shay'u ya'udduni'', when it burdens me, ''awdan''. End of quotation.

He only said "some room for consideration" because metathesis is well known in the language, so it is not far-fetched that ''wada'a'' is a transposition of ''ada''. Al-Murtada said: If someone asks: How is it valid to question one who has no sin and no intellect? What benefit is there in questioning her about that, and what is the wisdom in it? The answer is in two respects:

The first is that the intended meaning is that her killer is required to produce proof for her killing, and he is questioned about his killing of her, for what sin it was, by way of rebuke, censure and establishing the proof. So the killers here are the ones truly questioned, not the one who was killed, and she is questioned about only in a secondary sense. This follows the pattern of the saying: ''I asked for my right'', meaning I demanded it. Similar to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And fulfil the covenant, for the covenant will be questioned﴾ [Al-Isra': 34], meaning it will be demanded and will be accounted for.

The second respect is that the question is truly directed at her, by way of reproach to him, censure of him, and warning him that he has no proof for killing her. This follows the pattern of His saying, exalted is He, to 'Isa, peace be upon him: ﴿Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 116], as a form of rebuke to his people and establishing the proof against them. If it is said, on this second respect: How can one who has no intellect and no understanding be addressed and questioned? The answer is that some people held that the purpose of this statement, when it is to rebuke the doer and shame him and cause him distress at that time as a form of punishment, is not impossible, even if the buried girl has no understanding of it. For the address, though directed at her and aimed at her, is in reality meant for someone else. They said: This is like the case of a tyrant who beats a child of his, then turns to his child saying: You were beaten, what is your sin, and by what right did he consider this lawful against you? So his purpose is to rebuke the tyrant, not to address the child. The better view is that one should say about this: Children, although with regard to their intellects they are not required to be fully mature in order to reach the rewards that are due to them, (p-6071) just as the same is required in reaching reward, if goodness is evident and the community agrees that in the Hereafter, upon their entry into the Gardens, they will be in the most perfect states and the best conditions, and that their intellects will then be complete, then on this basis it is fitting for the address to be directed to the buried girl, because in that state she will be among those who understand and comprehend the address. And if the purpose of it is to rebuke the killer and establish the proof against him. End of quotation.

Al-Shihab said: The rebuke was established by al-Tibi, who explained that when the one who was wronged is questioned in the presence of the wrongdoer, and the crime is attributed to him rather than to the wrongdoer, this prompts the wrongdoer to reflect on his own condition and the condition of the one he wronged. Then he sees the innocence of the one who was wronged and that he himself is the one deserving punishment and torment. This is an indirect method, by way of allusion, and it is more eloquent than explicit statement. By istidraj (gradual leading) is meant following a path that leads to the goal by questioning one who is not guilty and attributing the sin to him, until the one from whom that proceeded is made clear, just as 'Isa was questioned rather than the unbelievers. This is a kind of rhetorical embellishment that is itself remarkable. End of quotation.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The phrase ﴿was killed﴾ [At-Takwir: 9] was used only on the basis that the speech is a report about her.

Note (tanbih):

Al-Suyuti said in ''al-Iklil'': In the verse there is the magnifying of the matter of wa'd (burying alive), which is the burying of children alive. Muslim narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about 'azl (coitus interruptus), and he said: "It is the hidden wa'd. And it is: ﴿When the buried infant girl is asked﴾." End of quotation.

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab concerning this verse that he said: "Qays ibn 'Asim came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah! I buried some of my daughters alive in the Jahiliyyah. He said: 'Free a slave on behalf of each of them.' He said: O Messenger of Allah! I am a man of camels. He said: 'Then slaughter a camel on behalf of each of them.'"

Al-Darimi narrated at the beginning of his Musnad that "a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah! We were a people of Jahiliyyah and idol worship, and we used to kill our children. I had a daughter, and when I called her she would answer, and she was delighted by my calling her. One day I called her and she followed me, and I passed on until I came to a well belonging to my family, not far away. I took her by the hand and threw her into the well, and the last I heard from her was her saying: 'O father, O father!'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wept until the tears flowed from his eyes. A man from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: You have grieved the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Be silent, for he is asking about what has distressed him." Then he said to him: "Repeat your story to me," and he repeated it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wept until the tears flowed from his eyes onto his beard. Then he said to him: "Allah has indeed removed from the Jahiliyyah what they did. So begin your deeds anew."

The Arabs had a variety of ways of burying daughters alive. Among them was one who, when his daughter reached six years of age, would say to her mother: Perfume her and adorn her, until I take her to her relatives by marriage. He would have dug a well for her in the desert. He would bring her to the well and say to her: Look into it. Then he would push her from behind and pour dirt over her until the well was level with the ground.

Among them was one who, when his wife drew near to childbirth, would dig a pit so that she could give birth at the edge of the pit. If she bore a girl, she would throw her into the pit, and if she bore a boy, she would keep him.

Sa'sa'ah ibn Najiyah ibn 'Iqal, the grandfather of al-Farazdaq ibn Ghalib, became well known for being among those who redeemed the buried girls in the Jahiliyyah, and he forbade their killing. It is said that he saved a thousand buried girls, and it is said less than that. Al-Farazdaq took pride in this in his saying:

Among us is the one who prevented the burying women, and gave life to the buried one, so she was not buried.

And in his saying also:

I am the son of 'Iqal, son of Layla, and Ghalib, and the one who frees the captive bound in fetters.
We had two elders: one of them was the owner of the grave, and the other an elder who protected people from every grave.
At a time when daughters were not allowed to live, and they were devoted to the idols around the Mudawwar.
I am the son of the one whose generosity turned away death, and no honour I defended was ever lacking.
My father was one of the two rains, Sa'sa'ah, who, whenever al-Jawza' and the star fail, sends rain.
He protected the daughters of those who buried, and whoever seeks protection at the grave will know that he does not betray.
And a woman who came to my father from a night of women, struggling with a wind whose night was not moonlit.
She said: Redeem for me what I have borne, for I have come to you from the poorest and needy of the camel-loads.
He saw the earth as a resting place for her, so he cast her down into cheeks of it, and into the worst of pits.
He said to her: Sleep, for you are under my protection, and for your daughter there is a protector from her father, the one with the wide forehead.

Abu 'Ubaydah narrated that "this Sa'sa'ah came as a delegate to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the delegation of Bani Tamim. He said: Sa'sa'ah had prevented burying in the Jahiliyyah, and he did not leave Tamim to bury their daughters, though he was able to do so. When Islam came, he had redeemed, according to some reports, four hundred buried girls, and according to another report three hundred. He said to the Prophet (ﷺ): May my father and mother be your ransom! Advise me. He said: "I advise you concerning your mother and father, your sister and brother, and your near ones, your near ones." He said: Increase it for me. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Guard what is between your jaws and your legs." Then he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "No deed has reached me from you except that it was done." He said: O Messenger of Allah! I saw the people surging in no clear direction, and I did not know where the right course was, except that I knew they were not upon it. I saw them burying their daughters, so I knew that their Lord, mighty and majestic, had not commanded them to do that, so I did not leave them, and I redeemed what I was able to."

It is said that once Jarir and al-Farazdaq gathered before Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik and boasted. Al-Farazdaq said: "I am the son of the one who gives life to the dead." Sulayman said to him: "You are the son of the one who gives life to the dead?" He replied: "My grandfather revived the buried daughter, and Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And whoever gives life to one, it is as if he had given life to all mankind﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 32], and my grandfather revived ninety-two buried daughters." Sulayman smiled and said: "You, with your poetry, are indeed a jurist (faqih)." Al-Murtada related it in his (Amali). In sum, burying daughters (al-wa'd) was a custom among the most abominable practices of the Jahiliyyah, which indicates the utmost cruelty, complete harshness and severity.

The Imam said: Look at this cruelty and hardness of heart, and the killing of innocent girls without any sin except fear of poverty and shame. How was it replaced with mercy and compassion after Islam mingled with the hearts of the Arabs? How great is the blessing of Islam upon all of humanity by its erasing this ugly custom. End of quote.

Among the fruits of this blessing is that the literati of the early generation began composing, in praise of daughters, verses more radiant than strings of pearls. Among them is the saying of Ma'n ibn Aws:

> I have seen men who dislike their daughters,
> while among them, let us not lie, are righteous women,
> and among them, while the days cause the youth to stumble,
> are servants who never tire of him, and mourners.

And al-'Alawi al-Jammani said, concerning a friend of his to whom a daughter was born and who was displeased with her, in verse:

> They said to him: "What have you been granted?" He listened, then said: "A daughter."
> Yet the greatest of those who have fathered women is the father of daughters, so why do you grieve, O two?
> Indeed, those whom you love among all creatures
> have gained, through the virtue of the daughter, what they have used to subdue their enemies with a crushing subjugation.

It is related that Amr ibn al-As entered upon Mu'awiyah while his daughter was with him. He said: "Who is this, O Mu'awiyah?" Mu'awiyah said: "This is the fruit of the heart, the sweet basil of the eye, and the fragrance of the nose." Amr said: "Remove her from you." He asked: "Why?" Amr said: "Because they give birth to enemies, bring near the distant, bequeath resentment, and stir up hatred." Mu'awiyah said: "Do not say that, O Amr! By Allah, nothing has soothed the sick, consoled the dead, aided against time, or dispelled the host of sorrows like them. You will find a maternal uncle whom his sister's sons have benefited, and a father whom the offspring of his sons have raised." Amr said: "O Mu'awiyah! I entered upon you while there was nothing on earth more hateful to me than them, and I leave from your presence while there is nothing on earth more beloved to me than them."

In a note to a companion congratulating him on the birth of a daughter: "Welcome and well come to the noble one among women, the mother of sons, the bringer of in-laws and pure offspring, and the herald of brothers who will be harmonious and noble youths who will follow one another:"

> Had women been like those we have found,
> women would have been preferred over men.
> The feminine gender of the word "sun" is no defect,
> nor is the masculine gender a glory for the "crescent."

May Allah the Exalted grant you blessing at its outset and happiness in its place. So put on joy and begin again with vigor. The world (al-dunya) is feminine, men serve it and males worship it. The earth is feminine, from it the creation was made and in it the offspring multiplied. The heaven is feminine, and it has been adorned with stars and decorated with the piercing star. The soul (al-nafs) is feminine, and it is the support of bodies and the essence of life. Life is feminine, and without it bodies would not move and humankind would not be known. Paradise is feminine, with it the righteous are promised and in it the messengers take delight. So congratulations to you, congratulations for what you have been given, and may Allah inspire you to thank Him for what you have been granted.

A note was copied for Abu al-Faraj al-Babbaghaa: News reached me of the fortunate newborn girl, may Allah honor her lineage and make her grow in goodly growth. As for your agitation upon receiving the news, and your denial of what Allah has chosen for you in the foreordained decree, you know that they are closer to the hearts, and that Allah began with them in the ordering, saying, Mighty is He who speaks: ﴿He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 49]. What Allah the Exalted has named a gift is more deserving of thanks and better suited to gracious acceptance. So may Allah congratulate you on the arrival of this noble one to you, and its fruit is the preparation of good offspring for you.

Anecdotes on this subject are countless, and all of them are from the blessing and virtue of Islam.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (*Mahasin al-Ta'wil*) on Surah 81, verses 1–9 (part 1 of 2):

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surat at-Takwir

It is also called the surah of ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾. It is Meccan, and its verses number twenty-nine.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn Umar that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look upon the Day of Resurrection as if he were seeing it with his own eyes, let him recite ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾ [Al-Infitar: 1] and ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq: 1]." At-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1–9] ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ ﴿And when the stars fall and scatter﴾ [At-Takwir: 2] ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾ [At-Takwir: 3] ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾ [At-Takwir: 4] ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [At-Takwir: 5] ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [At-Takwir: 6] ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [At-Takwir: 7] ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾ [At-Takwir: 8] ﴿for what sin she was killed﴾ [At-Takwir: 9]

﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: that is, it is removed from its place, cast off from its orbit, and its light is extinguished.

﴿And when the stars fall and scatter﴾ [At-Takwir: 2]: that is, they are scattered and plunge down.

﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾ [At-Takwir: 3]: that is, they are lifted from the surface of the earth and blown away, because of the quaking and the earthquake that shatters their joints.

﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾ [At-Takwir: 4]: that is, they are left neglected, with no herdsman and no one to claim them. ''Al-'Isharu'' is the plural of ''ushara'', which is a she-camel whose pregnancy has reached ten months. He singled them out because they are the most precious of their possessions. That is: when these pregnant animals, for which their owners compete, are neglected and left alone because of the severity of the terror that has descended upon them, then what of other things?!

﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [At-Takwir: 5]: that is, they are brought together from every side and mixed together, because the earthquake and the destruction have overtaken their dens and hiding places, so they come out bewildered and terrified, from the effect of the earthquake of the earth, and their joints are torn apart.

﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [At-Takwir: 6]: that is, they are filled by some of them being made to flow into others, until they become one single sea. It derives from ''sajjara al-tannur'', meaning he filled the oven with firewood. Like His saying: ﴿And when the seas are made to burst forth﴾ [Al-Infitar: 3]. It has also been said that the meaning is that they blaze into fire. Al-Qaffal said: It is possible that Hell lies in the depths of the seas, and it is not kindled now for the sake of the continuation of the world. When the term of the world is complete, God will convey the effect of those fires to the seas, and they will become entirely kindled because of that. Al-Imam clarified this by saying: Their being set ablaze may also mean their being ignited into fire. For what is within the belly of the earth of fire will appear at that time, through its splitting open and the tearing apart of its upper layers, while the water at that point turns into vapour, and nothing remains in the seas except fire. As for the belly of the earth containing fire, some reports have indicated this. It has been reported that "the sea is the covering of Hell," though this is not found in its authentic collections. Yet scientific research has established it, and the boiling of volcanoes, which are mountains of fire, bears witness to it. End of quotation.

Al-Razi said: Know that these six signs may occur at the beginning of the time of the destruction of the world, and they may also occur after the Resurrection has taken place. There is nothing in the wording that indicates either of the two possibilities. As for the remaining six, they are specific to the Resurrection. End of quotation.

﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [At-Takwir: 7]: that is, the spirits are joined to their bodies, or they are gathered together with their likes in good and evil, and they are classified into categories, so that each is gathered with those who resemble him, among the blessed and the wretched.

﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾ [At-Takwir: 8] ﴿for what sin she was killed﴾ [At-Takwir: 9]: meaning the daughters whom groups of the Arabs used to kill. Al-Sayyid al-Murtada said in his ''Amali'': The ''mawudah'' is the one who was killed while still young. The Arabs in the Jahiliyyah used to bury their daughters, by burying them alive. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Shall he keep it in disgrace, or bury it in the dust?﴾ [An-Nahl: 59], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those have lost who killed their children foolishly, without knowledge﴾ [Al-An'am: 140]. It is said that they used to do this for two reasons. One of them is that they would kill them out of fear of poverty. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not kill your children out of poverty﴾ [Al-An'am: 151]. Al-Murtada said: I found Abu 'Ali al-Jubba'i and others saying: She was only called ''mawudah'' because the dirt that was thrown upon her weighed her down until she died. In this there is some room for consideration, because they say from ''mawudah'' ''wada'a (yadi'u) wa'dan'', and the agent is ''wa'id'', and the feminine agent is ''wa'idah''. And from weight they say: ''ada'ni al-shay'u ya'udduni'', when it burdens me, ''awdan''. End of quotation.

He only said "some room for consideration" because metathesis is well known in the language, so it is not far-fetched that ''wada'a'' is a transposition of ''ada''. Al-Murtada said: If someone asks: How is it valid to question one who has no sin and no intellect? What benefit is there in questioning her about that, and what is the wisdom in it? The answer is in two respects:

The first is that the intended meaning is that her killer is required to produce proof for her killing, and he is questioned about his killing of her, for what sin it was, by way of rebuke, censure and establishing the proof. So the killers here are the ones truly questioned, not the one who was killed, and she is questioned about only in a secondary sense. This follows the pattern of the saying: ''I asked for my right'', meaning I demanded it. Similar to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And fulfil the covenant, for the covenant will be questioned﴾ [Al-Isra': 34], meaning it will be demanded and will be accounted for.

The second respect is that the question is truly directed at her, by way of reproach to him, censure of him, and warning him that he has no proof for killing her. This follows the pattern of His saying, exalted is He, to 'Isa, peace be upon him: ﴿Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 116], as a form of rebuke to his people and establishing the proof against them. If it is said, on this second respect: How can one who has no intellect and no understanding be addressed and questioned? The answer is that some people held that the purpose of this statement, when it is to rebuke the doer and shame him and cause him distress at that time as a form of punishment, is not impossible, even if the buried girl has no understanding of it. For the address, though directed at her and aimed at her, is in reality meant for someone else. They said: This is like the case of a tyrant who beats a child of his, then turns to his child saying: You were beaten, what is your sin, and by what right did he consider this lawful against you? So his purpose is to rebuke the tyrant, not to address the child. The better view is that one should say about this: Children, although with regard to their intellects they are not required to be fully mature in order to reach the rewards that are due to them, (p-6071) just as the same is required in reaching reward, if goodness is evident and the community agrees that in the Hereafter, upon their entry into the Gardens, they will be in the most perfect states and the best conditions, and that their intellects will then be complete, then on this basis it is fitting for the address to be directed to the buried girl, because in that state she will be among those who understand and comprehend the address. And if the purpose of it is to rebuke the killer and establish the proof against him. End of quotation.

Al-Shihab said: The rebuke was established by al-Tibi, who explained that when the one who was wronged is questioned in the presence of the wrongdoer, and the crime is attributed to him rather than to the wrongdoer, this prompts the wrongdoer to reflect on his own condition and the condition of the one he wronged. Then he sees the innocence of the one who was wronged and that he himself is the one deserving punishment and torment. This is an indirect method, by way of allusion, and it is more eloquent than explicit statement. By istidraj (gradual leading) is meant following a path that leads to the goal by questioning one who is not guilty and attributing the sin to him, until the one from whom that proceeded is made clear, just as 'Isa was questioned rather than the unbelievers. This is a kind of rhetorical embellishment that is itself remarkable. End of quotation.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The phrase ﴿was killed﴾ [At-Takwir: 9] was used only on the basis that the speech is a report about her.

I took her by the hand and threw her into the well, and the last I heard from her was her saying: 'O father, O father!'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wept until the tears flowed from his eyes. A man from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: You have grieved the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Be silent, for he is asking about what has distressed him." Then he said to him: "Repeat your story to me," and he repeated it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wept until the tears flowed from his eyes onto his beard. Then he said to him: "Allah has indeed removed from the Jahiliyyah what they did. So begin your deeds anew."

He would have dug a well for her in the desert. He would bring her to the well and say to her: Look into it. Then he would push her from behind and pour dirt over her until the well was level with the ground.

Among us is the one who prevented the burying women, and gave life to the buried one, so she was not buried.

And in his saying also:

I am the son of 'Iqal, son of Layla, and Ghalib, and the one who frees the captive bound in fetters.
We had two elders: one of them was the owner of the grave, and the other an elder who protected people from every grave.
At a time when daughters were not allowed to live, and they were devoted to the idols around the Mudawwar.
I am the son of the one whose generosity turned away death, and no honour I defended was ever lacking.
My father was one of the two rains, Sa'sa'ah, who, whenever al-Jawza' and the star fail, sends rain.
He protected the daughters of those who buried, and whoever seeks protection at the grave will know that he does not betray.
And a woman who came to my father from a night of women, struggling with a wind whose night was not moonlit.
She said: Redeem for me what I have borne, for I have come to you from the poorest and needy of the camel-loads.
He saw the earth as a resting place for her, so he cast her down into cheeks of it, and into the worst of pits.
He said to her: Sleep, for you are under my protection, and for your daughter there is a protector from her father, the one with the wide forehead.

He said to the Prophet (ﷺ): May my father and mother be your ransom! Advise me. He said: "I advise you concerning your mother and father, your sister and brother, and your near ones, your near ones." He said: Increase it for me. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Guard what is between your jaws and your legs." Then he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "No deed has reached me from you except that it was done." He said: O Messenger of Allah! > I have seen men who dislike their daughters,
> while among them, let us not lie, are righteous women,
> and among them, while the days cause the youth to stumble,
> are servants who never tire of him, and mourners.

And al-'Alawi al-Jammani said, concerning a friend of his to whom a daughter was born and who was displeased with her, in verse:

> They said to him: "What have you been granted?" He listened, then said: "A daughter."
> Yet the greatest of those who have fathered women is the father of daughters, so why do you grieve, O two?
> Indeed, those whom you love among all creatures
> have gained, through the virtue of the daughter, what they have used to subdue their enemies with a crushing subjugation.

It is related that Amr ibn al-As entered upon Mu'awiyah while his daughter was with him. He said: "Who is this, O Mu'awiyah?" Mu'awiyah said: "This is the fruit of the heart, the sweet basil of the eye, and the fragrance of the nose." Amr said: "Remove her from you." He asked: "Why?" Amr said: "Because they give birth to enemies, bring near the distant, bequeath resentment, and stir up hatred." Mu'awiyah said: "Do not say that, O Amr! By Allah, nothing has soothed the sick, consoled the dead, aided against time, or dispelled the host of sorrows like them. You will find a maternal uncle whom his sister's sons have benefited, and a father whom the offspring of his sons have raised." Amr said: "O Mu'awiyah! I entered upon you while there was nothing on earth more hateful to me than them, and I leave from your presence while there is nothing on earth more beloved to me than them."

In a note to a companion congratulating him on the birth of a daughter: "Welcome and well come to the noble one among women, the mother of sons, the bringer of in-laws and pure offspring, and the herald of brothers who will be harmonious and noble youths who will follow one another:"

> Had women been like those we have found,
> women would have been preferred over men.
> The feminine gender of the word "sun" is no defect,
> nor is the masculine gender a glory for the "crescent."

May Allah the Exalted grant you blessing at its outset and happiness in its place. So put on joy and begin again with vigor. The world (al-dunya) is feminine, men serve it and males worship it. The earth is feminine, from it the creation was made and in it the offspring multiplied. The heaven is feminine, and it has been adorned with stars and decorated with the piercing star. The soul (al-nafs) is feminine, and it is the support of bodies and the essence of life. Life is feminine, and without it bodies would not move and humankind would not be known. Paradise is feminine, with it the righteous are promised and in it the messengers take delight. So congratulations to you, congratulations for what you have been given, and may Allah inspire you to thank Him for what you have been granted.

So may Allah congratulate you on the arrival of this noble one to you, and its fruit is the preparation of good offspring for you.

﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: that is, it is removed from its place, cast off from its orbit, and its light is extinguished.

''Al-'Isharu'' is the plural of ''ushara'', which is a she-camel whose pregnancy has reached ten months. He singled them out because they are the most precious of their possessions. That is: when these pregnant animals, for which their owners compete, are neglected and left alone because of the severity of the terror that has descended upon them, then what of other things?!

﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [At-Takwir: 5]: that is, they are brought together from every side and mixed together, because the earthquake and the destruction have overtaken their dens and hiding places, so they come out bewildered and terrified, from the effect of the earthquake of the earth, and their joints are torn apart.

It has also been said that the meaning is that they blaze into fire. When the term of the world is complete, God will convey the effect of those fires to the seas, and they will become entirely kindled because of that. For what is within the belly of the earth of fire will appear at that time, through its splitting open and the tearing apart of its upper layers, while the water at that point turns into vapour, and nothing remains in the seas except fire. And in his saying also:

I am the son of 'Iqal, son of Layla, and Ghalib, and the one who frees the captive bound in fetters.
We had two elders: one of them was the owner of the grave, and the other an elder who protected people from every grave.
At a time when daughters were not allowed to live, and they were devoted to the idols around the Mudawwar.
I am the son of the one whose generosity turned away death, and no honour I defended was ever lacking.
My father was one of the two rains, Sa'sa'ah, who, whenever al-Jawza' and the star fail, sends rain.
He protected the daughters of those who buried, and whoever seeks protection at the grave will know that he does not betray.
And a woman who came to my father from a night of women, struggling with a wind whose night was not moonlit.
She said: Redeem for me what I have borne, for I have come to you from the poorest and needy of the camel-loads.
He saw the earth as a resting place for her, so he cast her down into cheeks of it, and into the worst of pits.
He said to her: Sleep, for you are under my protection, and for your daughter there is a protector from her father, the one with the wide forehead.

> I have seen men who dislike their daughters,
> while among them, let us not lie, are righteous women,
> and among them, while the days cause the youth to stumble,
> are servants who never tire of him, and mourners.

> They said to him: "What have you been granted?" He listened, then said: "A daughter."
> Yet the greatest of those who have fathered women is the father of daughters, so why do you grieve, O two?
> Indeed, those whom you love among all creatures
> have gained, through the virtue of the daughter, what they have used to subdue their enemies with a crushing subjugation.

> women would have been preferred over men.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surat at-Takwir

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn Umar that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look upon the Day of Resurrection as if he were seeing it with his own eyes, let him recite ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾ [Al-Infitar: 1] and ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq: 1]." At-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: that is, it is removed from its place, cast off from its orbit, and its light is extinguished.

﴿And when the stars fall and scatter﴾ [At-Takwir: 2]: that is, they are scattered and plunge down.

﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾ [At-Takwir: 3]: that is, they are lifted from the surface of the earth and blown away, because of the quaking and the earthquake that shatters their joints.

﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾ [At-Takwir: 4]: that is, they are left neglected, with no herdsman and no one to claim them. ''Al-'Isharu'' is the plural of ''ushara'', which is a she-camel whose pregnancy has reached ten months. He singled them out because they are the most precious of their possessions. That is: when these pregnant animals, for which their owners compete, are neglected and left alone because of the severity of the terror that has descended upon them, then what of other things?!

﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [At-Takwir: 5]: that is, they are brought together from every side and mixed together, because the earthquake and the destruction have overtaken their dens and hiding places, so they come out bewildered and terrified, from the effect of the earthquake of the earth, and their joints are torn apart.

﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [At-Takwir: 6]: that is, they are filled by some of them being made to flow into others, until they become one single sea. It derives from ''sajjara al-tannur'', meaning he filled the oven with firewood. Like His saying: ﴿And when the seas are made to burst forth﴾ [Al-Infitar: 3]. It has also been said that the meaning is that they blaze into fire. Al-Qaffal said: It is possible that Hell lies in the depths of the seas, and it is not kindled now for the sake of the continuation of the world. When the term of the world is complete, God will convey the effect of those fires to the seas, and they will become entirely kindled because of that. Al-Imam clarified this by saying: Their being set ablaze may also mean their being ignited into fire. For what is within the belly of the earth of fire will appear at that time, through its splitting open and the tearing apart of its upper layers, while the water at that point turns into vapour, and nothing remains in the seas except fire. As for the belly of the earth containing fire, some reports have indicated this. It has been reported that "the sea is the covering of Hell," though this is not found in its authentic collections. Yet scientific research has established it, and the boiling of volcanoes, which are mountains of fire, bears witness to it. End of quotation.

[15–21] The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted:

﴿So I swear by the retrogrades﴾ [al-Takwir: 15] ﴿the runners that run and hide﴾ [al-Takwir: 16] ﴿and by the night when it departs﴾ [al-Takwir: 17] ﴿and by the morning when it breathes﴾ [al-Takwir: 18] ﴿that this is the word of a noble messenger﴾ [al-Takwir: 19] ﴿endowed with power, with standing before the Lord of the Throne﴾ [al-Takwir: 20] ﴿obeyed there, and trustworthy﴾ [al-Takwir: 21]

﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالخُنَّسِ﴾ means: the receding ones among the stars, from khanasa (khunus), meaning he returned and moved back. Al-Zamakhshari said: "You see a star at the end of its mansion (burj), then it turns back and returns to its beginning."

﴿الجَوارِ﴾ [al-Takwir: 16] is the plural of jariyah, from al-jarya (running). ﴿الكُنَّسِ﴾ [al-Takwir: 16] means: those that hide, which enter their mansions as seen by the eye, from kanasa al-wahsh, when the wild animal entered its kinās, which is its den made of tree branches. It is originally a metaphor through the mode of comparison, then by common usage it became a literal term.

﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا عَسْعَسَ﴾ [al-Takwir: 17] means: it turned back and only a little remained, and that is the time of predawn (suhur).

﴿والصُّبْحِ إذا تَنَفَّسَ﴾ [al-Takwir: 18] means: it came forward and became clear, or its gentle breeze blew, or the distress and gloom of the night were lifted from it, in comparison to one who has his distress relieved (naffasa 'anhu karbahu). Al-Imam said: God the Exalted swore by these luminaries to highlight their status from the aspect of what their movements contain of signs of the power of the One who directs and decrees them, and of guidance by those movements to what their existence contains of wondrous craftsmanship and perfect order, together with describing them in the oath by what distances them from the ranks of divinity, namely receding and hiding, as a rebuke to those who singled them out for worship and took them as lords besides Him. In the night when it turns back is the removal of that gloom which overwhelms living beings, with the spreading of darkness after bodies had regained their vigor and revived from their lethargy. In the morning when it breathes is the good news to souls of a new life in a new day, in which wills set off to attain desires, fulfil needs, make up for what was missed, and prepare for what is coming. End.

The answer to the oath is His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [al-Takwir: 19], meaning the Spirit of Holiness (ruh al-qudus) who breathes into his heart (ﷺ), and he is Jibril (peace be upon him). The pronoun refers either to the Resurrection and recompense, understood from His saying: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما أحْضَرَتْ﴾ [al-Takwir: 14], or to what was mentioned, namely this, or to the Qur'an. ﴿ذِي قُوَّةٍ﴾ means: possessing strength to bear the burdens of the message and for everything he is commanded with, as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿شَدِيدُ القُوى﴾ [al-Najm: 5]. ﴿عِنْدَ ذِي العَرْشِ مَكِينٍ﴾ [al-Takwir: 20] means: possessing standing, honour and a high rank with Him, the Exalted.

﴿مُطاعٍ ثَمَّ﴾ [al-Takwir: 21] means: in the Highest Assembly (al-mala' al-a'la). ﴿أمِينٍ﴾ [al-Takwir: 21] means: trusted with His revelation, the Exalted, and His message.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 81, verses 22–25:**

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[22–25] ﴿Your companion is not mad.﴾ ﴿And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon.﴾ [al-Takwir: 23] ﴿And he is not withholding about the unseen.﴾ [al-Takwir: 24] ﴿And it is not the word of an accursed devil.﴾ [al-Takwir: 25]

﴿Your companion is not mad.﴾ That is: he is not one who speaks out of possession and raves with the raving of madmen.

(p-6079) Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers. This is a denial of what his enemies slandered him with, (ﷺ), out of envy and baseness.

Al-Shihab said: In His saying ﴿your companion﴾ there is a rebuke to them in the most subtle manner, for it is an indication that he grew up among you from the beginning of his affair until now. So you know him best, and you know that he is the most complete of creation in intellect, the most excellent of them in nobility, and the most perfect and clear-minded of them in mind. Madness is ascribed to him only by one who is made up of foolishness and madness. How fine is al-Buhturi's saying:

"When my virtues, in which I take pride, become my sins, then tell me how I am to make excuse."

﴿And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon.﴾ That is: Muhammad (ﷺ) certainly saw Jibril on the high horizon, the one that makes manifest what he sees in it.

Ibn Kathir said: The apparent meaning, and God knows best, is that this surah was revealed before the night of the Isra' (the Night Journey), because it mentions in it only this vision, which is the first. As for the second, which is mentioned in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent,﴾ [al-Najm: 13] ﴿at the Lote-tree of the utmost boundary,﴾ [al-Najm: 14] ﴿near which is the Garden of Refuge.﴾ [al-Najm: 15] that one was mentioned in surah al-Najm, and it was revealed after surah al-Isra'.

The purpose of stating his seeing Jibril, peace be upon them both, in the form of a man, is to establish the revelation, and that his affair is based on direct witnessing and sight, not on conjecture and supposition. Whatever is of this kind, there is no room for doubt in it.

﴿And he is not withholding about the unseen.﴾ That is: he is not stingy.

Mujahid said: He does not withhold from you what he knows; that is, he does not withhold teaching and conveying. Al-Farra' said: (p-6080) the unseen of the heaven comes to him, and it is a precious thing, so he does not withhold it from you. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: The meaning is that he reports the unseen and makes it clear, and does not conceal it, as a soothsayer (kahin) conceals it and refrains from informing about it until he takes a gift (huluwan) for it. It has also been read as "bi-zanin" with the letter ẓā', meaning: he is not accused regarding what he reports of the unseen.

Al-Qashani said: Because the devil of imagination and the jinn of fancy cannot gain control over him, so his speech would not be mixed up, and the sacred meaning would not blend with the imaginary and fanciful. For his intellect was purified of any admixture of imagination. The meaning is that he is truthful in what he reports of the revelation, the Last Day, and the recompense; it is not in his nature to be accused of it. As Heraclius said to Abu Sufyan: "I asked you whether you used to accuse him of lying before he said what he said, and you claimed no. So I knew that he would not abandon lying about people and then go and lie about God."

Note:

Ibn Jarir said: In my view, the more correct of the two readings is the one whose written form is common to the copies of the Muslims' Qur'ans, even though their recitation differs in it. That is ﴿withholding﴾ [al-Takwir: 24] with the letter ḍād, because all of that is so in their written forms. The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who interpreted it as: "Muhammad, according to what God has taught him of His revelation and sending down, is not stingy in teaching it to you, O people; rather, he is eager that you believe in it and learn it." End of quotation. Abu 'Ubayda preferred the reading with ẓā' for two reasons:

The first: the disbelievers did not accuse him of stinginess; they accused him (of lying), so denying the accusation is more fitting than denying stinginess.

The second: His saying ﴿about the unseen﴾ [al-Takwir: 24]. If the meaning were stinginess, He would have said "bi-l-ghaybi" (with the unseen), because one says "so-and-so is stingy with such-and-such" (ḍanīn bi-kadhā), and it is rarely said "ʿalā kadhā" (upon such-and-such).

Al-Shihab said: In al-Nashr [Ibn al-Jazari] said: it is with the letter ḍād in all the copies of the Qur'an. This does not conflict with Abu 'Ubayda's view that the letters ḍād and ẓā' in the old script do not differ except by the addition of a small stroke at the head of one of them over the other, (p-6081) a slight addition which may cause confusion. That is correct, and whoever reads the musnad script (the old Arabic script) knows it. There is no accusation in this against the transmitters of the copies of the Qur'an, as some have imagined, because what they transmitted agrees with the mutawatir recitation (the recitation transmitted by a multitude so that they cannot agree on falsehood). What Abu 'Ubayda mentioned is necessary, because they stipulated for the recitations agreement with the 'Uthmanic orthography (rasm), and without that the recitation with ẓā' would contradict it. End of quotation.

Ibn Kathir said: Both readings are mutawatir, and their meaning is sound, as has been mentioned before.

﴿And it is not the word of an accursed devil.﴾ That is: it is not from the inspiration of the devil who has been driven away from reaching this station. This is a denial of their saying that he is a soothsayer (kahanah).

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 81, verses 22–25:**

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[22–25] ﴿Your companion is not mad.﴾ ﴿And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon.﴾ [al-Takwir: 23] ﴿And he is not withholding about the unseen.﴾ [al-Takwir: 24] ﴿And it is not the word of an accursed devil.﴾ [al-Takwir: 25]

﴿Your companion is not mad.﴾ That is: he is not one who speaks out of possession and raves with the raving of madmen.

(p-6079) Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers. This is a denial of what his enemies slandered him with, (ﷺ), out of envy and baseness.

Al-Shihab said: In His saying ﴿your companion﴾ there is a rebuke to them in the most subtle manner, for it is an indication that he grew up among you from the beginning of his affair until now. So you know him best, and you know that he is the most complete of creation in intellect, the most excellent of them in nobility, and the most perfect and clear-minded of them in mind. Madness is ascribed to him only by one who is made up of foolishness and madness. How fine is al-Buhturi's saying:

"When my virtues, in which I take pride, become my sins, then tell me how I am to make excuse."

﴿And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon.﴾ That is: Muhammad (ﷺ) certainly saw Jibril on the high horizon, the one that makes manifest what he sees in it.

Ibn Kathir said: The apparent meaning, and God knows best, is that this surah was revealed before the night of the Isra' (the Night Journey), because it mentions in it only this vision, which is the first. As for the second, which is mentioned in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent,﴾ [al-Najm: 13] ﴿at the Lote-tree of the utmost boundary,﴾ [al-Najm: 14] ﴿near which is the Garden of Refuge.﴾ [al-Najm: 15] that one was mentioned in surah al-Najm, and it was revealed after surah al-Isra'.

The purpose of stating his seeing Jibril, peace be upon them both, in the form of a man, is to establish the revelation, and that his affair is based on direct witnessing and sight, not on conjecture and supposition. Whatever is of this kind, there is no room for doubt in it.

﴿And he is not withholding about the unseen.﴾ That is: he is not stingy.

Mujahid said: He does not withhold from you what he knows; that is, he does not withhold teaching and conveying. Al-Farra' said: (p-6080) the unseen of the heaven comes to him, and it is a precious thing, so he does not withhold it from you. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: The meaning is that he reports the unseen and makes it clear, and does not conceal it, as a soothsayer (kahin) conceals it and refrains from informing about it until he takes a gift (huluwan) for it. It has also been read as "bi-zanin" with the letter ẓā', meaning: he is not accused regarding what he reports of the unseen.

Al-Qashani said: Because the devil of imagination and the jinn of fancy cannot gain control over him, so his speech would not be mixed up, and the sacred meaning would not blend with the imaginary and fanciful. For his intellect was purified of any admixture of imagination. The meaning is that he is truthful in what he reports of the revelation, the Last Day, and the recompense; it is not in his nature to be accused of it. As Heraclius said to Abu Sufyan: "I asked you whether you used to accuse him of lying before he said what he said, and you claimed no. So I knew that he would not abandon lying about people and then go and lie about God."

Note:

Ibn Jarir said: In my view, the more correct of the two readings is the one whose written form is common to the copies of the Muslims' Qur'ans, even though their recitation differs in it. That is ﴿withholding﴾ [al-Takwir: 24] with the letter ḍād, because all of that is so in their written forms. The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who interpreted it as: "Muhammad, according to what God has taught him of His revelation and sending down, is not stingy in teaching it to you, O people; rather, he is eager that you believe in it and learn it." End of quotation. Abu 'Ubayda preferred the reading with ẓā' for two reasons:

The first: the disbelievers did not accuse him of stinginess; they accused him (of lying), so denying the accusation is more fitting than denying stinginess.

The second: His saying ﴿about the unseen﴾ [al-Takwir: 24]. If the meaning were stinginess, He would have said "bi-l-ghaybi" (with the unseen), because one says "so-and-so is stingy with such-and-such" (ḍanīn bi-kadhā), and it is rarely said "ʿalā kadhā" (upon such-and-such).

Al-Shihab said: In al-Nashr [Ibn al-Jazari] said: it is with the letter ḍād in all the copies of the Qur'an. This does not conflict with Abu 'Ubayda's view that the letters ḍād and ẓā' in the old script do not differ except by the addition of a small stroke at the head of one of them over the other, (p-6081) a slight addition which may cause confusion. That is correct, and whoever reads the musnad script (the old Arabic script) knows it. There is no accusation in this against the transmitters of the copies of the Qur'an, as some have imagined, because what they transmitted agrees with the mutawatir recitation (the recitation transmitted by a multitude so that they cannot agree on falsehood). What Abu 'Ubayda mentioned is necessary, because they stipulated for the recitations agreement with the 'Uthmanic orthography (rasm), and without that the recitation with ẓā' would contradict it. End of quotation.

Ibn Kathir said: Both readings are mutawatir, and their meaning is sound, as has been mentioned before.

﴿And it is not the word of an accursed devil.﴾ That is: it is not from the inspiration of the devil who has been driven away from reaching this station. This is a denial of their saying that he is a soothsayer (kahanah).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 81, verses 26–29:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[26–29] ﴿So where are you going?﴾ ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾ [at-Takwir: 27] ﴿for whoever among you wills to take the straight path﴾ [at-Takwir: 28] ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds﴾ [at-Takwir: 29]

﴿So where are you going?﴾ That is: what path are you taking, when the proof has been established against you? Undoubtedly you are turning away from guidance after these claims concerning the Revelation and its bearer. Whoever takes its ways has strayed far from what is correct, in a manner that does not restrain him and does not bring him near to it in any way, like one who takes a path that takes him away from the direction of his destination, so it is said to him: "Where are you going?"

Al-Zamakhshari said: This is a rebuke to them, as one says to someone who abandons the main road and goes off in a crooked or winding way: "Where are you going?" Their condition is likened to his condition, in their abandoning of the truth and their turning away from it toward falsehood.

﴿It is not but﴾ [at-Takwir: 27], that is, the Qur'an recited to you, ﴿a reminder to the worlds﴾ [at-Takwir: 27], that is, a reminder and admonition for them.

The Imam said: It is an admonition by which they remember what Allah has placed in their natures of inclination toward good; what has made them forget this reminder is the evil dispositions that have come upon their natures, which are produced by the diseases of society. And His saying, exalted is He:

﴿for whoever among you wills to take the straight path﴾ [at-Takwir: 28] is a substitution from "the worlds," that is: it is a reminder for whoever intends to be steadfast upon the true path, by directing his will and inclination toward it and remaining firm upon it. As for whoever turns away and withdraws, (p-6082) how can the reminder benefit him, when the rust (ran) has increased him in blindness?

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds﴾ [at-Takwir: 29], that is: you do not will any of your actions except that Allah wills to enable you to exercise your will, to empower you to do them, and to leave you free to do them. The benefit of this statement is the informing of dependence upon Allah, exalted is He, and that the servant has no power over what Allah has not decreed; he is subject to the authority of His will, subdued under His governance and His determination.
